thought
The test image shows a mango leaf with dark, splotchy fungal growth on its surface. The leaf itself appears to be yellowish-green underneath the dark areas. This strongly suggests Sooty Mould. I will read the `part_index.md` file to confirm that all possible classes affect the leaf, and then start viewing reference images, prioritizing Sooty Mould.

thought

Now, I will view the first reference image for Anthracnose.

thought
The reference image for Anthracnose (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a young, brownish leaf with significant damage and holes, which is distinctly different from the test image. The test image shows superficial dark growth, not tissue damage and discoloration like this Anthracnose image.

Next, I will view the first reference image for Die_Back.

thought
The reference image for Die_Back (`Mango_Leaf_166.jpg`) shows a completely dried, brown, and curled leaf. This is very different from the test image, which has green-yellow areas and a superficial dark growth.

Now, I will view the first reference image for Powdery_Mildew.

thought
The reference image for Powdery_Mildew (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a leaf covered with white, powdery spots, which is distinctly different from the dark, sooty appearance of the test image.

Based on the initial round of viewing one image from each class, Sooty_Mould is the strongest candidate. I have used 4 out of 16 views. I will now use the remaining 12 views to confirm my prediction by viewing more Sooty Mould images, and then systematically viewing other candidates to rule them out further.

I will view the remaining two Sooty Mould images, then two more Anthracnose, then two more Die_Back, and then two more Powdery_Mildew images. After that, I will use the remaining 4 views to revisit the strongest candidates or to further rule out others.
